scope: Phase C only; visual assessment of still reference, not production approval or timed playback

groups.label: HEAD VARIATION (IDLE)
groups.kind: head studies, 2 rows × 5; temporal order unknown
groups.strengths: Compact void inside an irregular hot envelope; unequal tips avoid a symmetrical flame badge.
groups.problems: Paired bright spots read as eyes; void width/tilt varies; no body attachment or loop exposures.
groups.learn: Independent shape variation can suggest unstable self-image.
groups.do_not_copy: Eye dots, skull silhouette, any flame contour, or the two-row arrangement.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Head envelope is legible; a neck attachment is absent.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: N/A body; void width and apparent head volume vary across the ten studies.
assessment.Center of gravity: N/A body; head/root registration is unspecified.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Dark center and bright envelope read clearly; tiny internal spots read as facial features.
assessment.Line of action: Unequal tips give local upward/diagonal gestures.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: No defined action start; these may be alternatives rather than anticipations.
assessment.Recovery quality: No demonstrated return to a source shape.
assessment.Limb arcs: No limbs; flame-tip paths cannot be tracked through unregistered alternatives.
assessment.Spacing: No temporal spacing metadata; board intervals are layout.
assessment.Frame rhythm: Unknown exposures and loop seam; two rows are not proof of two cycles.
assessment.Action readability: Reads as a flaming face, partly through eye-like points that conflict with the brief.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Body absent; no lag or phase offset can be established.
assessment.Smear logic: No explicit smear; changes are silhouette alternatives.
assessment.Smear source/destination: No registered source/destination for a deformation.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Hot rim and internal light spots can form eye sockets; some tips join into a crown.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Void tilt/width and tip count drift; deliberate variation versus volume error is unresolved.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Clear hot/dark contrast at board scale; source is not proof at the game's 56-pixel body height.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Asymmetric tips feel chosen; repeated eye-faced fire heads feel conventional. Provenance unknown.

groups.label: HEAD DURING ACTION
groups.strengths: Directional stretching and compact-to-elongated contrast; trailing tips connect to a main mass.
groups.problems: No anatomical root or return shape; void becomes a missile-like leading face; eye-like dots remain.
groups.learn: Secondary shape deformation can communicate direction without diffuse glow.
groups.do_not_copy: Meteor heads, leading eye-faced void, exact streaks, or presumed frame order.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Head mass remains identifiable, but no neck/body attachment is supplied.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: N/A body; apparent head length and void volume change substantially.
assessment.Center of gravity: N/A body support; leading void has no registered body reference.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Compact versus elongated forms are distinct; the long forms read as projectiles.
assessment.Line of action: Clear directional diagonals and horizontal pulls.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: No body initiator; cannot identify what preceded each stretch.
assessment.Contact clarity: N/A impact; no target or body contact.
assessment.Recovery quality: Return to a contained head is not shown as an ordered beat.
assessment.Limb arcs: No limbs; trailing tip direction is visible, not a proven tracked arc.
assessment.Spacing: Temporal spacing unknown; gaps between sketches are not travel distance.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No durations, hold counts, or repeat metadata.
assessment.Action readability: Strong directional flame; ambiguous whether it is a head deformation or launched attack.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: No body, so lag is a possible principle rather than a verified phase relation.
assessment.Smear logic: Broad hot mass and attached trailing lobes form an intelligible smear vocabulary.
assessment.Smear source/destination: Compact and long examples suggest possible endpoints, but registration/order and contraction are missing.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Long red tails can detach visually; hot bridges sometimes narrow around the void.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Void and envelope enlarge together instead of preserving a stable head anchor.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Directional mass reads at board scale; eye details and attached-root read at game scale remain unverified.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Directional silhouettes are purposeful; meteor/fireball associations must be rejected.

groups.label: IDLE
groups.kind: body poses; trailing ellipsis outside count
groups.strengths: Low shoulders, wide support, uneven flame tips, quiet clothing.
groups.problems: Last pose turns frontal; slight silhouette breathing is mixed with orientation changes; limb and neck continuity unclear.
groups.learn: A quiet support stance lets local asymmetry and head instability remain visible.
groups.do_not_copy: Slouched hoodie figure, wide trouser/sneaker proportions, frontal snap, or five-pose sequence.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Arms attach plausibly in the first four; last frontal view changes limb visibility.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Baggy volumes are broadly similar; torso/shoulder widths change with the last orientation.
assessment.Center of gravity: Weight appears between separated feet; no pronounced transfer is evidenced.
assessment.Foot planting: Soles appear planted; root alignment and actual pinning cannot be measured from montage positions.
assessment.Ground contact: Common illustrated baseline, with small shoe-height differences.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Wide trouser/feet mass reads; hanging hands can merge with the jacket.
assessment.Line of action: Shallow slouch rather than a distinctive whole-body action.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: N/A sustained idle; no entry anticipation supplied.
assessment.Contact clarity: N/A combat contact; support is apparent at both shoes.
assessment.Recovery quality: Last frontal pose does not establish a continuous return to the first.
assessment.Limb arcs: Small hand/shoulder differences cannot define continuous joint arcs.
assessment.Spacing: Small body differences precede a larger facing change; actual timing unknown.
assessment.Frame rhythm: Five visible alternatives/poses; no breathing exposure or loop seam evidence.
assessment.Action readability: Idle reads, but mostly through a familiar relaxed stance.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Flame tips vary while support stays quiet; no measured delayed response.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Hands/hem/outer trouser edges often meet without a clear separating gap.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Possible shoulder/neck/hand drift; facing changes could explain some differences.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Broad stance and flame read at board scale; fine cuff/shoe texture is weak and runtime fit untested.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Quiet body against changing head is useful; stock slouch and last-view discontinuity are weak.

groups.label: WALK
groups.strengths: Forward intention, some heel/toe variation, muted body versus active head.
groups.problems: Mostly repeated wide stride; no unambiguous passing/crossover or opposite-leg support; body resembles a slow run.
groups.learn: Separate support and travel direction when evaluating a gait.
groups.do_not_copy: Repeated lunge gait, limb ambiguity, exact contact shapes, or a new walk mechanic.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Elbows/hands change visibility; near/far limb ownership is not consistently trackable.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Similar torso mass but hand and shoe sizes drift in their textured outlines.
assessment.Center of gravity: Torso projects forward; support transfer between legs is not demonstrated clearly.
assessment.Foot planting: Rear heel/toe changes are visible; no convincing full plant-to-release sequence per foot.
assessment.Ground contact: Front soles repeatedly meet the line; timing of contact is unknown.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Open stride is readable but passing silhouettes are missing.
assessment.Line of action: Repeated forward lean with little independent pelvis/shoulder change.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: N/A action windup; contact/down/passing/high progression is incomplete.
assessment.Contact clarity: Multiple contact-like feet, without a clearly paired opposite contact.
assessment.Recovery quality: No established repeatable return or complete opposite half-stride.
assessment.Limb arcs: Arm pumping suggests motion; elbows and feet lack identifiable continuous ownership/arcs.
assessment.Spacing: Visible poses stay in a similar split stance; spatial spacing is unregistered.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No exposures; five drawings plus ellipsis cannot establish a cycle.
assessment.Action readability: Locomotion reads, but walk/run distinction and support rhythm are weak.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Tips rise/trail somewhat; flame-base changes are not tied to a clear planted beat.
assessment.Smear source/destination: N/A smear; no source/destination pair supplied.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Forward hand meets thigh/torso in several poses; inner-leg dark masses can merge.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Apparent hand/forearm and shoe changes risk flicker; cannot quantify without registered layers.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Leg split reads; small limb markers cannot rescue an unclear gait at game size.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Repeated stride templates and omitted passing poses feel generic; not proof of AI generation.

groups.label: RUN
groups.strengths: Strong forward pitch, bent knees, some apparent contact/flight changes, clear stride silhouette.
groups.problems: Opposite-half leg ownership unclear; repeated athletic lunge pattern; substantial hand/shirt changes; no seam proof.
groups.learn: A gait needs distinct support/flight silhouettes and stable limb ownership.
groups.do_not_copy: Hero sprint posture, six-frame recipe, trousers/shoes, or inferred mirrored half-cycle.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Arms and knees are broadly plausible; overlaps do not consistently identify the same limbs.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Torso mass is similar, but exposed shirt strip and hands change prominently.
assessment.Center of gravity: Forward COM suits travel; it is not shown transferring through a fully identifiable two-leg cycle.
assessment.Foot planting: Several soles appear planted and middle poses suggest flight; per-foot anchoring remains uncertain.
assessment.Ground contact: Some feet touch the line, others hover; this is descriptive, not a verified world trajectory.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Stride delta is strong, but most poses share the same diagonal wedge.
assessment.Line of action: Persistent athletic forward diagonal; shoulders and pelvis largely turn together.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: No run-entry windup supplied; cycle support beats are only partial.
assessment.Contact clarity: Contact-like poses are legible, but opposite-side contacts are not unambiguous.
assessment.Recovery quality: First/last poses differ; a continuous repeat cannot be inferred.
assessment.Limb arcs: Pump and knee lift are visible; near/far hand and foot arcs cannot be reliably traced.
assessment.Spacing: Pose differences imply compression/flight, but root-space distances and temporal spacing are absent.
assessment.Frame rhythm: Six visible drawings are not exposure counts; no three-loop or seam evidence.
assessment.Action readability: Run reads strongly; distinct protagonist-specific behavior does not.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Tips tend backward/upward; head silhouette remains similar through disparate support poses.
assessment.Smear logic: No explicit body smear; trailing small flame marks are decorative or secondary.
assessment.Smear source/destination: No registered stretched body/head source-to-destination event.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Fists merge into shirt/hip; rear arm can disappear into jacket mass.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Hand silhouette, shirt exposure, and limb overlap vary; possible flicker rather than designed foreshortening.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Broad motion reads at board scale; cloth speckle and limb identifiers will be fragile at game scale.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Readable sprint vocabulary, but generic athletic body language and ambiguous cycle construction.

groups.label: JUMP
groups.kind: standing, airborne and landing-related body poses
groups.strengths: Clear standing-to-tucked-to-low compression contrast; airborne and landing silhouettes differ.
groups.problems: No distinct launch coil; overlapping limbs lose ownership; ending stays compressed; illustration positions are not a trajectory.
groups.learn: Airborne compression and landing compression can differ from upright support.
groups.do_not_copy: Exact tuck, final crouch, stock parkour gesture, body proportions, or six-step arc.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Airborne legs overlap into one trouser mass; knees/feet are identifiable only intermittently.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Torso volume is broadly retained; compressed legs obscure actual bone lengths.
assessment.Center of gravity: Airborne mass folds under torso; landing shifts into a wide low base.
assessment.Foot planting: Planted shoes are visible at start/end; whether the same foot lands first is unresolved.
assessment.Ground contact: Start/end meet the drawn line; montage heights cannot establish physics.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Large upright-to-tuck-to-low delta is useful; tucks lose limb separation.
assessment.Line of action: Forward curling action rather than vertical extension; pelvis/shoulder sequencing unspecified.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: Starts standing; no clearly differentiated load-before-launch pose.
assessment.Contact clarity: Landing-related wide/low poses read, but exact first touchdown is not marked.
assessment.Recovery quality: Ends in deep compression, without a demonstrated return to neutral.
assessment.Limb arcs: Hands pull back and legs tuck; joint identity is lost through overlaps.
assessment.Spacing: Large silhouette changes are visible; root alignment and exposure spacing absent.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No apex hold, launch duration, or landing exposure metadata.
assessment.Action readability: Reads as jump/landing illustration; not a validated timed jump sequence.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Flame mostly follows head tilt and rises; delayed ascent stretch is not established.
assessment.Smear source/destination: N/A smear; exact launch/apex/landing registrations are absent.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Folded knees/shoes and hand/hip intersections close negative spaces.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Cloth bunching could explain volume changes; folded limb shortening still needs resolution.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Big tuck/compression reads; feet and hands merge at reduced scale; actual runtime fit untested.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Useful contrast among phases, but launch/recovery and paired anatomy lack authored precision.

groups.label: FALL
groups.strengths: Loose legs and low ending suggest loss of support.
groups.problems: First pose already grounded; middle feet project forward like a seated jump/kick; descent intent and landing recovery unclear.
groups.learn: Loss of support must be distinguishable from jumping or attacking.
groups.do_not_copy: Seated-flight sequence, claimed ballistic arc, overlapping legs, or generic upright flame.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Forward feet are readable, but seat-like leg arrangement obscures pelvis/knee relationships.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Torso appears similar while limb extension varies sharply; no landmarks prove consistent lengths.
assessment.Center of gravity: Mass leans behind extended feet in middle poses; support-loss direction is ambiguous.
assessment.Foot planting: No falling foot plant; grounded first/last poses are not a clear landing sequence.
assessment.Ground contact: Only illustrative low endpoints; row placement cannot prove descent.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Middle seated/kicking silhouettes differ from tuck, but do not clearly identify passive falling.
assessment.Line of action: Loose backward-seated line contrasts with other rows, without a clear descending body intent.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: N/A ordinary fall anticipation; grounded opening makes support loss hard to locate.
assessment.Contact clarity: No unambiguous first touchdown; last pose is a low collapsed mass.
assessment.Recovery quality: No release from landing compression or return shown.
assessment.Limb arcs: Foot extension is visible; near/far-leg transitions cannot be traced cleanly.
assessment.Spacing: Montage moves up then down on the board; this cannot be interpreted as velocity.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No ordered duration/hold data or transition into fall.
assessment.Action readability: Could read as hop, kick, seated flight, or fall; action distinction is weak.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Mostly upright flame tips; upward drag versus body descent is not demonstrated.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Extended shoe/other leg and hand/hip intersections muddle limb edges.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Sudden leg visibility/length changes may be overlap or unintended distortion.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Extended shoes read at board scale, but small-size fall identity is not established.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Generic seated airborne poses; weak distinction from jump and hurt.

groups.label: DASH
groups.kind: similar low body poses with increasing flame stretch
groups.strengths: Low travel line; flame tails align backward while body aims forward.
groups.problems: Almost fixed lunge anatomy; final void/flame becomes huge; no exit or reconnection; body identity overshadowed.
groups.learn: Directional secondary deformation can make a brief motion read.
groups.do_not_copy: Flame rocket, escalating head size, repeated crouched cutout, or four-step ramp.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Low arms and folded front leg are broadly plausible; overlaps hide joints.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Body varies less than head; the last head/void expands far beyond prior proportions.
assessment.Center of gravity: COM pitches over the front knee; no distinct load/release or exit transfer.
assessment.Foot planting: Both shoes often appear on the line despite implied travel; static montage cannot prove sliding.
assessment.Ground contact: Low body stays near the drawn baseline; ground and air dash are not separated.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Speed silhouette is clear; huge final head dominates the body.
assessment.Line of action: Horizontal forward thrust stays almost unchanged across the four body poses.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: No clear separate entry load; first pose already at low dash level.
assessment.Contact clarity: N/A strike contact; no dash landing/exit contact shown.
assessment.Recovery quality: No contraction, exit, or restored head-body relationship.
assessment.Limb arcs: Little body articulation; foot/hand continuity is too weak to establish a dash arc.
assessment.Spacing: Head stretch increases, but corresponding displacement/exposures are unknown.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No hold/exposure metadata; cannot map four drawings onto the game's 150 ms.
assessment.Action readability: Reads as low rush becoming a fire-headed missile.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Backward tails are directionally coherent; measured delay from the body is absent.
assessment.Smear logic: Broad elongated hot mass is legible; late enlargement is a different apparent head volume.
assessment.Smear source/destination: Early contained head is a possible source; no clear registered destination/restoration.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Tail crosses shoulders and neckline; hot/void boundary can swallow the attachment.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Last void/head grows radically, while body changes little.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Bright streak reads at small board scale, but body mechanics become secondary; runtime read unknown.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Useful directional contrast, weak whole-body authorship and excessive flame dominance.

groups.label: ATTACK 1 (QUICK)
groups.kind: guard-like poses, reach, raised-arm pose and leaning ending
groups.strengths: Forward arm extension and some torso turn create a recognizable strike-like gesture.
groups.problems: Repeated early guards; unclear striking-hand continuity; raised-arm/lifted-foot excursion; no clean source return.
groups.learn: The striking surface and body's support must remain readable through contact.
groups.do_not_copy: Generic punch/combo sequence, alternating hand ambiguity, exact pose angles, or fixed six frames.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Reach arm reads in pose 4; subsequent raised arms and crossing hands obscure limb ownership.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Torso turn changes shirt exposure; fist and limb silhouettes vary across gestures.
assessment.Center of gravity: Wide base then lifted leg changes support abruptly; COM-to-support transition unclear.
assessment.Foot planting: First poses show planted shoes; later lifted leg lacks a demonstrated replant/recovery.
assessment.Ground contact: Most poses meet the line; raised-foot beat interrupts that support.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Extended arm creates a strong delta; early poses are near-duplicate guards.
assessment.Line of action: Progresses from forward hunch to diagonal reach, then a different raised gesture.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: Several similar early stances lack a strong isolated coil.
assessment.Contact clarity: Pose 4 suggests reach/contact, but there is no marked contact beat or stable hand anchor.
assessment.Recovery quality: Last pose remains pitched with arm back; no continuity to opening guard established.
assessment.Limb arcs: Hands appear to switch roles; no reliable single striking-hand arc.
assessment.Spacing: Three similar guards precede large changes; lack of durations prevents a rhythm judgment.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No exposures, contact hold or return timing; cannot fit directly to 50/120/80 ms windows.
assessment.Action readability: Strike-like, but may be a combo/raised swing rather than one clear quick melee.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Flame tilt varies with head; delayed shear at hand contact is not established.
assessment.Smear logic: Small hot streak near the raised reach is ambiguous: hand effect, flame or incidental mark.
assessment.Smear source/destination: No clearly rooted smear connecting one striking hand to a destination.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Raised forearm/hot marks meet the face; guarded fists merge with torso.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Fist scale, arm visibility and lifted-leg transition may cause unintended popping.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Reach reads at board scale; individual hands/contact must survive the game's smaller body.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Familiar punch poses; insufficient support, hand and recovery continuity for a reusable motion plan.

groups.label: ATTACK 2 (HEAVY)
groups.kind: low stance, head arc, enlarged head thrust and partial return
groups.strengths: Large compression/stretch contrast and one readable broad horizontal flame mass.
groups.problems: Flame/void becomes the apparent weapon; small body change under giant smear; recoil lacks a stable return; no heavy action exists in current game.
groups.learn: One decisive silhouette change can express impact better than disconnected texture.
groups.do_not_copy: Headbutt/fire projectile, giant void, heavy-attack mechanic, exact flame arc or sequence.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Body stays in a plausible low split stance; hands do not identify a consistent striking surface.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Body/head proportion breaks at the huge elongated void.
assessment.Center of gravity: Forward bias increases in the long-head pose without a clear body-support transfer.
assessment.Foot planting: Shoes mostly repeat wide support shapes; true foot pinning unknown.
assessment.Ground contact: Baseline is broadly maintained in the montage.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Smear silhouette is powerful but overwhelms torso/hand information.
assessment.Line of action: Forward rush and horizontal head stretch; torso/pelvis contribution is limited.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: First low pose may load action; the second flame arc is stronger than body anticipation.
assessment.Contact clarity: Longest head form suggests an attack peak, but body/weapon contact is not identifiable.
assessment.Recovery quality: Last pose reduces the head shape but returns to a different arm/body gesture.
assessment.Limb arcs: Hand/shoulder arcs are weakly differentiated; head envelope is the main visible arc.
assessment.Spacing: Large change occurs between arc and elongated head; no registered distances or times.
assessment.Frame rhythm: Four samples, no exposures; no separate heavy timing may be added to gameplay.
assessment.Action readability: Reads as a head-led fiery charge more than current ordinary melee.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Head exaggeration exceeds body reaction; phase is dominated by apparent flame power.
assessment.Smear logic: Connected hot envelope gives a solid mass, but its leading void looks projectile-like.
assessment.Smear source/destination: Contained head and long head exist; attachment and restored destination do not remain stable.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Long envelope blankets neck/shoulder and merges into body contour.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Head volume expands dramatically rather than remaining a anchored deformation.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Flame dominates at board size; damage surface and body action become obscure.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Spectacular effect carries a generic low lunge; incompatible as the game's motion blueprint.

groups.label: ATTACK 3 (UP)
groups.kind: low load, rising arms, overhead flame arc, forward sweep and partial recovery
groups.strengths: Strong low-to-tall silhouette contrast and a broad curved flame sweep.
groups.problems: No upward attack exists; apparent strike direction shifts forward; arm/flame ownership unclear; strong spell/aura association.
groups.learn: A curved deformation can communicate a directional change when properly rooted.
groups.do_not_copy: Uppercut/new attack, overhead fire arc, upright hero pose, exact five-sample progression.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Rise arms are plausible in isolation; later low arms do not define one consistent striking limb.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Height changes through crouch/rise; body volumes cannot be verified through overlaps.
assessment.Center of gravity: Base stays wide while torso rises; later forward pitch changes support intent.
assessment.Foot planting: Wide soles mostly touch line; which foot pivots or accepts load is unknown.
assessment.Ground contact: Floor line is broadly respected, except height changes from poses cannot establish a trajectory.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Low-to-tall-to-low change is strong; hot arc can conceal hand action.
assessment.Line of action: Starts rising, then becomes horizontal; upward intent does not remain singular.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: First low pose is a readable preparation, unlike several other attack rows.
assessment.Contact clarity: Peak overhead arc does not identify an upward body/weapon contact surface.
assessment.Recovery quality: Final forward lean is not a neutral return; next-state continuity unproven.
assessment.Limb arcs: Flame arc is apparent; hand path changes/overlaps obscure an anatomical arc.
assessment.Spacing: Large height and direction changes with no registered frame spacing.
assessment.Frame rhythm: Five sketches, unknown exposures; gameplay has no matching upward damage window.
assessment.Action readability: Could read as uppercut, fire spell, or sweep; unsupported for the current move set.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Hot arc accompanies arm rise then head rush; actual delayed secondary behavior unproven.
assessment.Smear logic: Curved hot strip is broad, but reads like an external attack effect.
assessment.Smear source/destination: No unequivocal attachment to head/hand across all samples or settled destination.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Overhead hot strip touches wrist/head; later trail merges into shoulder.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Flame envelope expands into a separate arc, obscuring whether the head remains attached.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Arc reads loudly at board scale; hand/support meaning loses priority at game scale.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Readable contrast but familiar heroic spell/uppercut language; must not become a new move.

groups.label: HURT
groups.kind: guard/lean variations followed by one lifted-leg low reaction
groups.strengths: Last low, unbalanced pose breaks the usual wide stance; head tips briefly scatter laterally.
groups.problems: Early poses resemble attack guards; impact direction unspecified; no restored support; frontal torso shift and limb ownership need review.
groups.learn: A reaction must differ from attack preparation and show interrupted support.
groups.do_not_copy: Guard sequence, lifted-foot kick read, exact knockback pose, or added input-lock/recovery time.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Arms remain broadly attached; middle crossing arms and final legs are hard to assign.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Torso turns toward front, then folds; overlap explains some apparent volume changes.
assessment.Center of gravity: Final mass shifts over one supporting leg, unlike preceding wide stances.
assessment.Foot planting: Final foot lifts visibly; no replant is shown.
assessment.Ground contact: Support shoe stays near line; actual knockback trajectory cannot be inferred.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Final low silhouette differs; first three resemble generic combat readiness.
assessment.Line of action: Small guarded leans then a large forward curl; impulse direction is unspecified.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: N/A intentional attack anticipation; early guards do not clearly show a received hit.
assessment.Contact clarity: No visible source/impact marker; one cannot locate exact reaction onset.
assessment.Recovery quality: No return or settled hurt exit supplied.
assessment.Limb arcs: Final leg changes sharply; continuous reaction limb paths are absent.
assessment.Spacing: Several small changes precede a large last gesture; temporal spacing unknown.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No exposure data; existing nonfatal visual clock is only 120 ms and must remain unchanged.
assessment.Action readability: Last beat reads off-balance, but also resembles a kick; hurt identity is incomplete.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Late lateral tip scatter may suggest disruption; body-to-flame delay not measured.
assessment.Smear source/destination: N/A smear; fragmentation lacks a proven source and reconnection beat.
assessment.Accidental tangents: Guarded hands overlap chest; bent knees and hips merge into one dark region.
assessment.Unintended deformation: Arm prominence and last-leg visibility change; could be occlusion or deformation drift.
assessment.Gameplay-scale readability: Large off-balance gesture reads; fine fingers/face and early guards do not assure small-size hurt clarity.
assessment.Authorship/genericity cues: Useful interrupted support idea; otherwise ordinary guard gestures with weak impact authorship.

groups.label: DEATH
groups.kind: 4 body-collapse poses + 1 ember-only sample; trailing ellipsis
groups.strengths: Progressive loss of height, hands approaching support, final prone mass, diminishing flame.
groups.problems: Near/far legs merge; body disappears in final sample without a dissolution rationale; contact timing and final mass anchoring unknown.
groups.learn: Loss of bodily support and loss of head structure can carry the ending.
groups.do_not_copy: Kneeling/prone pose sequence, corpse disappearance, ember/particle effect, or gameplay freeze.

assessment.Anatomy consistency: Descending torso and hands are plausible; folded knees/arms merge strongly.
assessment.Body proportion consistency: Apparent torso mass largely survives four body poses; fifth omits the entire body.
assessment.Center of gravity: Mass lowers from kneel toward floor and forearm/hand support.
assessment.Foot planting: Shoe remnants remain behind; hands appear to join support before prone endpoint.
assessment.Ground contact: Lower silhouettes broadly meet the line; registration and first torso contact unverified.
assessment.Silhouette readability: Height collapse is clear; intermediate dark folds lose separate limb read.
assessment.Line of action: Downward forward curl into horizontal rest.
assessment.Anticipation clarity: N/A attack anticipation; fatal impulse/start trigger is not shown.
assessment.Contact clarity: Hand/body-to-floor support is suggested, but no timed first contact.
assessment.Recovery quality: N/A live recovery; stable corpse/rest state is undermined by ember-only disappearance.
assessment.Limb arcs: Hand-to-floor path is suggested; folded leg and arm continuity needs anatomical proof.
assessment.Spacing: Progressive lowering then body removal; no exposure/settle metadata.
assessment.Frame rhythm: No durations; must respect existing 1.2 s reload without changing controller behavior.
assessment.Action readability: Death/collapse reads well through four poses; fifth could be dissolution rather than mere flame loss.
assessment.Flame/body phase relationship: Flame shortens toward floor as support collapses; exact lag and final extinction timing unknown.
assessment.Smear logic: No connected motion smear; final small sparks are separate marks.
assessment.Smear source/destination: N/A body smear; no demonstrated physical source for disappearing body mass.
